title: How Java resolves overloaded methods
answer: Java first identifies applicable overloads from the compile-time argument types, then applies method-invocation conversion rules and chooses the most specific applicable method. Exact matches are preferred over conversions where the language rules establish a more specific candidate; widening, boxing or unboxing, and varargs can participate according to the specification. AeroTopo's `join(String,int)` and `join(String,Integer)` demonstrate exact primitive versus wrapper matches.
